chunks: And by his chain, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who gives charity of a slave girl to his children while they are young. Then, if he is pleased with the slave girl while they are young dependents under his care, does he see it appropriate that he takes possession of her, or evaluates her at a just price, and calls witnesses to testify to her price upon him, or does he leave all of that and not deal with any of it? He (peace be upon him) said: He evaluates her at a just price, and reckons her price as being for them (the children) upon himself, and he may take possession of her.
ai.seo_question: Can a father keep a slave girl he gave as charity to his young children?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the mechanism of 'Istibdaal' (exchange) in Islamic jurisprudence, where a father retains a gifted slave by compensating the children with a just valuation treated as a debt on himself. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on fairness in family transactions, ensuring the children's property rights are preserved even when the parent exercises practical control. The ruling underscores the principle that retaining a gift requires formalizing the transaction to prevent unjust enrichment at the expense of the minors.
